title: Design System: tuan photography 陳亮元

display.purpose: Page titles, the home page line, the name of a guide shown as a feature, the Instagram handle in the footer.

headline.purpose: Section headings, headings inside a guide, the place name in the viewer, country names in the destinations index.

title.purpose: Continent names in the index, the name under a tile, the heading of the quick facts card.

lead.purpose: The flowing list of place names without work, and plain rows.

body.purpose: Reading text. Paragraphs in a guide are at most 40rem wide. Emphasis is weight 600. Chinese line-height 1.9.

small.purpose: Tables, dates under a title, captions, the contents list, viewer data.

caption.purpose: The second line of a caption, camera data, the footer's small print. Tabular lining figures.

capitals.purpose: The menu, the language switch, buttons, the breadcrumb, table header cells. Set in capitals. In Chinese: 0.875rem with 0.14em spacing.

scrims.name: opening-photograph-top
scrims.purpose: Keeps the site name and menu readable in paper white on the opening photograph. Used nowhere else.

scrims.name: opening-photograph-bottom
scrims.purpose: Keeps the small place line readable on the opening photograph. Used nowhere else.

motion.name: out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve, used by every transition and arrival.

motion.name: settle-opening
motion.purpose: The opening photograph settling into place once on arrival.

motion.name: uncover-lead
motion.value: 1100ms clip from the top edge, with a 1600ms settle
motion.purpose: The lead photograph at the top of a guide being uncovered on arrival.

motion.name: rise-words
motion.value: 900ms, opacity 0 to 1 and 1.5rem upward, delay 200ms plus 90ms per item
motion.purpose: The words under a title coming up after the photograph: home intro, guide title block, About.

motion.name: rise-in-view
motion.purpose: Photographs in a wall, features, tiles and doors rising as they enter the window. Only where the browser supports it.

motion.name: photograph-hover
motion.purpose: A photograph enlarging very slightly inside its own frame under the pointer.

motion.name: door-hover
motion.purpose: A door brightening under the pointer.

motion.name: button
motion.value: 260ms background, border, colour; 1px down when pressed

motion.name: link
motion.purpose: Links and word controls changing colour under the pointer.

motion.name: picked
motion.purpose: A photograph travelling from its row to the viewer.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every arrival, rise, transition and view transition is switched off.

themes.note: Light only. The stylesheet declares color-scheme: light and there is no dark theme in this build.

chinese.punctuation: full-width, applied by zh_punct in tools/build.py

fonts.delivery: Google Fonts (open decision: hosting with the site)

narrative.overview:
The site is a travel journal set like a printed magazine. It opens with one photograph that fills the whole window, with no headline, no sentence and no button on it. After that, everything is quiet: place names and headings in a serif, centred; reading text in a plain sans; the menu and the buttons in small spaced capitals; all of it on warm paper. The owner chose this direction on 2026-09-28, naming Along Dusty Roads and The Common Wanderer as the template, a warm light ground, and the whole site.

The site is light only. The stylesheet declares `color-scheme: light` and there is no dark theme in this build. Visitors whose devices are set to dark still see the warm paper site.

Colour is used in two ways. The ground alternates between warm paper and a slightly darker stone band, section by section. Three earth colours (clay, olive and slate) appear as flat blocks: the three doors on the home page and the footer. Links and hover states are a deep clay. There are no icons: every control is a word.

Photographs are shown bare. In a row they keep their own shape and are never trimmed; their names sit beneath them, never on them. Opening any photograph shows it whole, with the account of how it was made beside it.
keyCharacteristics: One opening photograph fills the window; nothing is written across it.
Warm paper and a stone band alternate by section. Light only.
Serif for names and headings, centred. Plain sans for reading. Small spaced capitals for the menu, buttons and labels.
Clay, olive and slate as flat blocks: three doors and the footer.
Every corner is square. Buttons are rectangles with capital labels.
Photographs are bare and untrimmed in rows, with captions beneath.
No icons. Every control is a word, in both languages.
Both languages are first-class. Chinese has its own sizes, spacing, weight and punctuation.
Motion has two reasons only, arriving and walking the wall, and all of it stops under "reduce motion".

rules.name: The Light Only Rule
rules.body: The site has one theme, light, on warm paper. There is no dark theme and no theme switch. A dark version would be a new decision for the owner, not an extension of this system.

rules.name: The Paper And Stone Rule
rules.body: Sections alternate between Warm Paper and Stone. A change of ground is how one section is told from the next; there are no boxes drawn around sections and no rules between them.

rules.name: The Flat Block Rule
rules.body: Clay, Olive and Slate are used as whole flat blocks with Paper White lettering: the three doors and the footer. They are not used for text on paper, for borders, for tints or for gradients. The build has two small exceptions for Clay, recorded under Open Decisions.

rules.name: The One Link Colour Rule
rules.body: Deep Clay is the only colour that means "this can be followed". It appears on links in reading text and on hover. It is never used as a fill at rest.

rules.name: The Plain Name Rule
rules.body: A title is the place's name: "Barcelona", "Spain", "Europe". Descriptive detail goes in the small line under it.

rules.name: The Serif For Names Rule
rules.body: The serif is for names and headings, and they are centred. Reading text, tables, labels and controls are sans. The serif is not used for paragraphs, except the one opening paragraph on About.

rules.name: The Words Not Icons Rule
rules.body: Controls are words: "Menu", "Previous", "Next", "Close", "Read the guide", "Map". There are no icons, arrows or pictograms on controls anywhere in the build.

rules.name: The Real Figures Rule
rules.body: Camera data, times, dates and prices use tabular lining figures, and every camera value shown is read from the photograph's own file. The capture clock time is not shown.

rules.name: The Quiet Punctuation Rule
rules.body: No long dashes in either language: a dash that introduces becomes a colon, one that adds on becomes a comma, and ranges use a plain hyphen. At most one middle dot in a line; a list of places reads as a list, with commas. The build applies this to every string (`no_dash_en`, `no_dash_zh`, `few_dots` in `tools/build.py`).

rules.name: The Two Languages Rule
rules.body: Every string exists in English and in 繁體中文, and neither is a translation afterthought. Nothing ships in one language only.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No shadows. Separation is made with a change of ground first, space second, and a 1px hairline third.

rules.name: The Two Reasons Rule
rules.body: Something moves only when the visitor arrives or when a photograph comes into view, plus the small answers to the pointer. Nothing loops, nothing moves on its own, and all of it stops under "reduce motion".

dos: Do keep the opening photograph clear: the top bar and one small place line are the only lettering on it.
Do show photographs bare, with their names beneath them.
Do let `rows_of()` lay out any row of photographs, so each row fills the column and no photograph is trimmed.
Do call a place by its plain name, and put detail in the small line under it.
Do write every string in both languages, and set Chinese by its own rules: open line-height, weight 500 serif, full-width punctuation.
Do alternate paper and stone to tell sections apart.
Do use clay, olive and slate as whole flat blocks with Paper White lettering.
Do take every colour from the eleven tokens in the stylesheet.
Do label every control with a word.
Do set camera data, times, dates and prices in tabular lining figures, and show only values read from the photograph's file.
Do say plainly, in one sentence, when work does not exist yet.
Do keep all motion inside the "reduce motion" switch.
Do edit `data/site.json`, `content/` and `tools/build.py`, then rebuild; the HTML pages are written out by the build.
donts: Don't write a headline, a sentence, a button or a panel across the opening photograph. The owner asked for this on his original site because the words blocked the image.
Don't set names, labels or badges on top of any photograph.
Don't trim a photograph in a row to make a grid even.
Don't frame, round, border or shadow a photograph.
Don't add a dark theme or a theme switch.
Don't add icons, arrows or pictograms to controls.
Don't add shadows, or gradients other than the two on the opening photograph.
Don't use clay, olive or slate for reading text or as tints.
Don't put a small capital line above a heading as decoration. The only line that sits above a title is the breadcrumb, and it is made of real links.
Don't add a third typeface, or bold the serif in English.
Don't add motion that loops or plays on its own.
Don't use long dashes, or more than one middle dot in a line.
Don't fill an empty place with a stand-in image, an invented guide, invented camera data, or a claim the site cannot yet support.

openDecisions.name: Typeface hosting
openDecisions.body: Playfair Display, Geist, Noto Serif TC and Noto Sans TC load from Google Fonts on every page. Hosting the files with the site needs the owner's permission to download them. The families are in use; how they are delivered is not decided.

openDecisions.name: About biography
openDecisions.body: The text on the About page is copy carried over from the previous site and has not been confirmed by the owner as his own words. It is not a model for the site's voice.

openDecisions.name: Contact email
openDecisions.body: No email address is published anywhere on the site. Whether to publish one is undecided.

openDecisions.name: Destinations lead sentence and continent taglines
openDecisions.body: The sentence under "Destinations" ("Every place I've photographed, researched, eaten through, and written up") and the one-line taglines for continents he has not yet visited (Africa, Antarctica, South America) read as claims the site cannot yet support: 15 of 16 countries have no guide, and those continents have no trips. They are the owner's copy to confirm or change.

openDecisions.name: The guide's "SIM / data" fact
openDecisions.body: It has no value yet. The build leaves the row out of the page until he supplies one, so the quick facts card shows only facts that have answers.

openDecisions.name: Carried from the product notes
openDecisions.body: which country gets the next guide, and whether a newsletter sign-up is wanted.

openDecisions.name: Where a photograph is trimmed
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: Two places, not three. The opening photograph is fitted to the window, so its edges are trimmed to the window's shape (on a phone held upright, a good deal of its width). Tiles on continent pages are fitted to a 3 by 2 opening. The feature photograph is not trimmed; it keeps its own shape, as do the guide's lead photograph, the quick facts photograph and every photograph in a row. The whole photograph is always available in the viewer. Neither trim is a licence to trim elsewhere.

openDecisions.name: The hover enlargement
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: A photograph grows 2% inside its frame under the pointer, which hides a sliver of its edges for that moment.

openDecisions.name: Clay outside the blocks
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: The stylesheet's own rule says clay, olive and slate appear only as flat blocks. Clay is also the ground of selected text and the underline beneath index names that have work. Both are small and built; they are not a reason to use the earth colours as accents.

openDecisions.name: The breadcrumb on continent pages
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: There it holds one word ("Destinations") in small capitals above the title, and at a glance it looks like a decorative label. It is a working link back to Destinations. It is recorded as navigation only.

openDecisions.name: Rising on scroll
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: It depends on a browser feature that not every browser has. Where it is missing, photographs are simply in place.

openDecisions.name: The browser's bar colour
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: Each page sets it with a typed value (`#f7f2e9`) in `tools/build.py`. It is a close match to Warm Paper, not taken from the token.

openDecisions.name: The darkening on the opening photograph
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: Its colour is typed into the stylesheet and is not one of the eleven tokens.

openDecisions.name: Unused helpers
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: The stylesheet defines two small helpers (`.caps`, `.quiet`) that no page uses at present.

openDecisions.name: Placeholder titles
openDecisions.status: recorded as built, not a rule to extend
openDecisions.body: The Skills page lists three planned articles and says on the page that their titles are placeholders.
